title: throughput-regression-continuous-batching-debug-scratchpad-9
body:
Context:
- Regression observed in production on 2024-11-11 17:40 UTC: sustained throughput drop (~30%) for model endpoints using continuous batching. Latency SLOs still met for p50 but p95 increased for a subset of requests.
- Affected stack: serving-runtime v2.7.1, continuous-batcher v1.3.0, kv-cache enabled (default TTL 10m), autoscaler policy: target-util 0.75, min-pods 4, max-pods 20.

What I saw (quick notes):
- Spike in request arrival variance (more high-variance short requests mixed with long ones). Batching behavior changed: fewer large batches formed, more small batches (<=2 requests) observed.
- Continuous batcher logs show repeated warnings about "batcher: flush timeout reached" and increased number of flush events.
- Prom metrics: batch_size_avg dropped from ~8.6 to ~3.1 over the regression window. tokens/sec decreased ~28%. CPU on inference pods unchanged; GPU utilization dropped proportionally.

Commands I ran locally / in prod: (timestamps in log snippets are UTC)
- kubectl logs -n inference batcher-xyz -c continuous-batcher --since=2h
  Output snippet:
    2024-11-11T17:38:45Z batcher INFO: accepted request req=abc123 size=512
    2024-11-11T17:38:45Z batcher WARN: flush timeout reached batch_id=42 waiting=120ms
    2024-11-11T17:38:46Z batcher DEBUG: emitted batch size=1 latency=1.2ms

- curl -s http://internal-metrics/endpoint/batcher | jq '.batch_size_histogram'
  Output: {"0-1": 0.41, "2-4": 0.44, "5-8": 0.12, ">8": 0.03}  (compared to pre-regression ~ {"0-1":0.12, "2-4":0.32, "5-8":0.36, ">8":0.20})

- kubectl exec -n inference -c runtime -- /bin/sh -c "curl -s localhost:9000/kvcache/stats"
  Output:
    hits: 1254
    misses: 9421
    evictions: 221
    size_rows: 134
    ttl_seconds: 600
  Observation: miss rate spiked; cache size still small (maybe frequent evictions).

- git diff of recent rollout (serving-runtime):
  changes: change in default batching window from 100ms -> 75ms in PR 456 (rollback candidate).

Error snippets / logs collected:
- "batcher WARN: flush timeout reached" repeated ~3k times during the window.
- "runtime WARN: kvcache miss for prefix xyz... falling back to recompute"
- "autoscaler INFO: scaling up to 12 pods due to CPU spike" (but CPU didn't spike on GPUs; autoscaler uses CPU-only metric in that config, so noisy).

Hypotheses (ordered by likelihood):
1) Batching window reduction + increased variance in request arrival -> smaller batches -> lower GPU throughput. The 75ms window makes the batcher flush earlier under variance.
2) KV-cache miss storm due to TTL/eviction pattern: misses cause additional compute per request and higher tail latency for some requests, causing more inter-arrival jitter and preventing batching from forming.
3) Autoscaler config mismatch: using CPU-based autoscaling for GPU-backed pods caused scale-up/down oscillation -> more cold starts of GPUs or model warmup leading to transient throughput drops.
4) A subtle change in kernel selection path (unlikely but flagged by runtime team) on v2.7.1 for certain seq len distributions.

Evidence for hypothesis 1:
- Recent PR changed batching window default (see linked PR). Rollback to previous 100ms config in canary environment reproduced larger batches and restored throughput to baseline. Local A/B test with 100ms vs 75ms: 100ms median batch size 7.8 tokens/sec 32k, 75ms batch size 3.4 tokens/sec 23k.

Evidence for hypothesis 2:
- KV cache miss rate increased starting 17:35 UTC. Misses correlate with higher per-request compute time in logs. Cache size small (134 rows) and evictions non-zero -> maybe keying change or cache partitioning bug.

Quick experiments I ran:
- Canary rollback of batcher window to 100ms on 10% of traffic -> batch size recovered to ~7, throughput improved ~18% for that slice. No immediate impact on key-value cache stats.
- Disabled kv-cache on a canary model instance -> p95 improved slightly but batch formation still poor.
- Switched autoscaler to GPU-metrics (experimental) for a single deploy -> no immediate beneficial effect; requires longer run.

Immediate action items (short-term mitigations):
- Rollback default batching window to 100ms cluster-wide (pending ops approval) — high confidence this will recover a large portion of throughput.
- Increase KV cache capacity / decrease eviction aggressiveness temporarily for affected model pool to reduce miss storm.
- Change autoscaler to use combined GPU metric (or guard with cooldown) to avoid scaling oscillation.

Longer-term follow-ups (post-mortem & fixes):
- Add integration test that simulates high variance arrival and verifies batch_size distribution does not regress when batching window changes.
- Investigate kv-cache keying logic and partitioning; add telemetry to correlate cache misses with specific request prefixes.
- Make batching window configurable per-model (we already have flag but need better defaults per seq length).
- Add canary safety: when changing batching defaults, run traffic-split experiments to measure batch size and tokens/sec automatically; block rollouts if drop > 10%.

Notes / TODOs for myself:
- Collect a full hour of continuous-batcher metrics and upload to Confluence page (CONFLUENCE-1234).
- Ask Marco to run profiling on GPU kernels for requests that had longer seq len patterns.
- Janelle to own KV-cache capacity bump and monitor miss rate.
- Draft postmortem draft with timeline + minimal repro steps.

Rough timeline:
- 17:30 UTC: first 5% traffic shows batch_size reduction
- 17:35 UTC: kv-cache miss spike appears
- 17:38 UTC: batcher flush timeouts increase heavily
- 17:45 UTC: throughput down ~28%
- 18:00 UTC: canary rollback (100ms) -> partial recovery for 10% traffic slice

Attach / reference logs:
- Collected logs: /var/log/ci/batcher-2024-11-11.tar.gz (uploaded to incident channel)
- Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.internal/d/serving/batching?from=2024-11-11T17:00:00Z&to=2024-11-11T19:00:00Z

Questions remaining / open decisions:
- Do we prioritize immediate rollback of batching window (disruptive) vs targeted per-model adjustments?
- How much KV cache capacity can Ops allocate quickly? (Janelle to confirm)
- Should autoscaler default switch to GPU metric for all GPU-backed pools? Need performance cost analysis.

If I get time next: collect detailed flamegraphs for single pod during miss storm and instrument batcher to log per-batch request IDs (sampling) to see correlation of request types and batch composition.

End of scratchpad.
